checks.release_startup_rejected: Error: "Blocked(\"filesystem not qualified for local claim slice\")"
checks.inherited_lock: Parent death retained lock; child exit released it
checks.isolated_startup: SIGTERM ended service and confirmed bootstrap child exit before server restoration; no SQLite or readiness
checks.outage: Metadata and source startup remained pending at 3-second observations
checks.restored: Stable root/namespace identity; metadata recovered and source lock became available

limitations: SLES 12 SP5 userspace on WSL2 kernel, not the SLES kernel or old CPU hardware.

Two container clients with distinct network/mount namespaces on one shared modern kernel. Ownership probes diagnose exclusion/missing-mount gaps; they do not prove physical-host fencing, partition/reclaim or safe takeover.

Real Rust cases cover selected claim, source-read, copy-write, verification-read, publication and claim/file/manifest-link points, including 180-second blocked claim and verification outages with live recovery. Claim/file-link crashes hold the local rendezvous during server outage and confirm two owned aliases before recovery; they do not model an in-flight unlink RPC. Longer or indefinite outages, queue saturation and export changes remain unqualified. Other lock/startup probes use OS tools.
Service startup rejection is measured; production NFS and source deletion remain disabled.
